subject: Contract discussion — availability SLAs, credits, and maintenance handoffs
messages:
From: Eileen Tan <eileen@cloudcorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Contract redlines — availability & maintenance

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached are the initial redlines our legal and procurement teams have flagged for the MSA + Order Form. The three items they want to resolve before we proceed are:

- Uptime target and service credit math: they want 99.95 for the Production tier and an automatic credit formula that escalates at 99.9 and 99.5.
- Response times: Acknowledgement / P1 / P2 time commitments that must be contractually defined (they expect 15 min ack for P1).
- Maintenance windows & blackout language: all planned maintenance must be limited to a weekly 4-hour window and any emergency maintenance must be notified 72 hours in advance where possible.

We included inline comments in CloudCorp_redlines_v1.pdf and linked the DocuSign placeholder so legal can see the proposed edits. We prefer to keep the SLA definitions tight since this is a regulated workload for a pilot.

Next step from our side: procurement would like a short redline response and a 30-minute call next week to close. Are you able to review and confirm what Redwood can accept as-is vs. where you need exceptions?

Thanks,
Eileen Tan
Sr. Procurement Manager, CloudCorp
[Attachment: CloudCorp_redlines_v1.pdf (9KB, pdf)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Eileen Tan <eileen@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract redlines — availability & maintenance

Eileen — thanks for the note and the PDF.

Marissa / Ben / Kim: looping you in for a quick read and to capture tradeoffs. High-level from product/ops: 99.95 sustained availability has meaningful cost and ops implications; we generally commit to 99.9 for our standard Production tier and offer 99.95 as a higher tier with reserved capacity. Also want to flag that the 72-hour notice for emergency maintenance is very constraining for patch security fixes.

Proposed internal next steps:
- Marissa: draft concession language (commercial) we can offer for the pilot — e.g., 99.9 baseline, 99.95 with Dedicated reservation + 90-day minimum commit.
- Ben: confirm what emergency maintenance notice we can guarantee and propose fallback language for security-critical patches.
- Kim: loop Legal to prepare the counter with clear credit calc.

I can join the call next Wed/Thu. Eileen — would Mar 11 or Aug 6 at 10:00 PT work for your team?

—Olga
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Eileen Tan <eileen@cloudcorp.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract redlines — availability & maintenance

Eileen — appreciate the clear asks. I've put together a short commercial compromise and attached a matrix that maps availability tiers to credit percentages and reserved capacity requirements. Highlights:

- Offer: 99.9 uptime for Production (no commit), service credits start at 99.7 (5%), 99.5 (15%), 99.0 (30%).
- Premium option: 99.95 with Dedicated reservation (min 3-month commit) and reduced credit exposure (1% / 5% / 10% bands).
- Response times: we can contract to 15-minute acknowledgement for P1 for the Dedicated tier, 1-hour for Production.
- Maintenance: propose a primary weekly 4-hour window (customer region local time) + a security exception clause allowing quicker patching with post-event notice and a commitment to reduce impact.

I will be on the call Aug 6 at 10:00 PT if that works — will bring a one-page commercial summary.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_opp_matrix.xlsx (12KB, xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Eileen Tan <eileen@cloudcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract redlines — availability & maintenance

Marissa / team — added some technical constraints so legal can draft workable language:

- Maintenance windows: our running maintenance cadence is flexible by region; we can commit to a "primary weekly 4-hour window" and a secondary window for failover systems. However, emergency security patches cannot always meet a 72-hour pre-notice; instead we propose "best-effort 72-hour notice; immediate application for critical patches with post-facto post-mortem and credit protection language limited to non-security incidents."
- Credits math: we recommend capping aggregated credit liability per billing cycle (e.g., max 100% of monthly bill for direct availability credits) — avoids open-ended exposure.
- Failover/fallback: suggest adding a clause that allows Redwood to route to a compatible model variant or region to maintain availability; credits apply only if both primary and fallback are unavailable.
- Response times: 15-minute ack for P1 on Dedicated only, include an escalation ladder: on-call -> engineering -> SRE manager within 60 minutes for production-impact incidents.

Ben (ops)
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

Eileen: we'll send a formal counter (commercial + technical summary) by EOD Tuesday with the credit cap language and the security exception wording Ben suggested. Kimberly, can Legal prepare a clean redline for DocuSign after we confirm the credit bands?

Confirmed call: Aug 6, 2025 10:00 PT (30 minutes) — agenda: 1) confirm uptime tiers & credits, 2) finalize maintenance exception language, 3) sign-off path (Legal + Procurement).

Olga
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
